questions.q: What is STIX, as described in this lesson?
options: A standardized JSON data model, maintained by OASIS, for describing threat intelligence objects and their relationships -- not a feed or product itself
A specific commercial threat-intelligence feed that competitors do not use
A Python library required to parse any threat-intel data
A replacement for TAXII that eliminates the need for an API
questions.explain: STIX is a data format/model, not a specific feed or tool -- many different sources produce data in STIX format, the same way many tools produce CSV.

questions.q: In a STIX indicator object, what does the `pattern` field actually contain?
options: A direct copy of a TAXII collection's URL
A base64-encoded binary signature
An expression written in STIX Patterning syntax, such as [ipv4-addr:value = '203.0.113.9'], identifying a detectable condition
A free-text description written by an analyst with no fixed syntax
questions.explain: The pattern field uses STIX Patterning, a small structured language for expressing detectable conditions like a specific IP address or file hash value.

questions.q: In the Python example that resolves STIX relationships, what is the purpose of building `objects_by_id = {obj["id"]: obj for obj in bundle["objects"]}`?
options: To send the bundle to a TAXII server over REST
To delete duplicate objects from the bundle
To convert the bundle from JSON into STIX Patterning syntax
To create a fast lookup table so relationship objects' source_ref and target_ref values can be resolved to the actual objects they point to
questions.explain: Indexing objects by their id lets the script quickly look up the full source and target objects referenced by a relationship object's source_ref and target_ref fields.

questions.q: What is the core distinction between STIX and TAXII, according to this lesson?
options: STIX only works with CSV files, while TAXII only works with JSON
TAXII defines the data model for threat intel objects, while STIX defines how to transport them over HTTP
STIX and TAXII are two names for the exact same standard
STIX is what you're sharing (the data model), while TAXII is how you ask for it (the transport/API standard)
questions.explain: The lesson states plainly: STIX is the data model being shared, and TAXII is the transport protocol/API standard used to request and exchange that STIX data.

questions.q: A STIX relationship object has relationship_type "uses", with source_ref pointing to a threat-actor object and target_ref pointing to a malware object. What does this relationship express?
options: There is no valid relationship type called "uses" in STIX
The threat-actor uses the malware
The malware uses the threat-actor's infrastructure
The malware object created the threat-actor object
questions.explain: source_ref identifies the subject of the relationship_type verb, and target_ref the object -- so source_ref (threat-actor) 'uses' target_ref (malware) means the threat actor uses that malware.
